_meta.description: Policy & fiscal forces acting on the universe — regime state (what the rules ARE right now), fiscal programs (who is paying whom), and levers to watch. Reconcile alongside the catalyst calendar; >60 days without reconciling = stale.

regimes.title: Export controls: tiered and whiplash-prone
regimes.state: Within twelve months Washington banned the H200, unbanned it (BIS rule effective Jan 16, 2026), then put a 25% tariff on it. Current shape: 'green-zone' chips (H20-class) flow freely, H200 sells under license + tariff, frontier GPUs stay banned. Jun 2026: BIS affirmed controls reach Chinese firms' overseas subsidiaries (closing the offshore loophole). Feb 2026: eight lawmakers pushed for a blanket WFE ban to China — entity-specific controls judged leaky. Aug 4 2026: the FCC is drafting an import ban on NEW MODELS of Chinese optical transceivers — the first time the control regime reaches past chips into datacenter networking hardware (rationale: data theft / malware / service-disruption risk). Officials hope to publish this year; it could still be modified or shelved.
regimes.watch: The regime changes with the political weather — that volatility, not any single rule, is the risk to price. NVDA/AMD China revenue swings on every revision; a blanket WFE ban would hit AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/8035.T's China backlogs.

regimes.title: Materials leverage: suspended, not dismantled
regimes.state: China built a 12-category rare-earth/critical-materials control regime through 2025 (gallium/germanium ~98% refined share, tungsten hexafluoride, electronic-grade HF, 'look-through' end-user tracing — domestic-vs-export price gaps up to 100x). The Oct 2025 escalation was SUSPENDED for one year at the Xi-Trump truce — expiring Nov 10, 2026. Separate controls now aimed at Japan.
regimes.watch: The Nov 10 expiry is a dated, binary event sitting under the robotics (magnets), optics (Ge/Ga) and fab-chemicals chains. Raw-materials names live in the Hard Assets sibling map — but the POLICY shock lands on this universe's act/opt/wfe verticals.

regimes.title: Substitution mandates + Big Fund capital
regimes.state: State-directed decoupling: domestic-substitution quotas push SMIC/NAURA/Cambricon/Empyrean into captive demand regardless of economics, funded by Big Fund III (~$50B) plus provincial money. Antitrust probes of US chipmakers held as a retaliation card.
regimes.watch: Makes the china-localization cohort (30 tagged names) partly policy-driven rather than market-driven — treat their revenue 'demand' accordingly in conviction terms.

fiscal_programs.who: TSM (Arizona), INTC (18A buildout + high-NA), MU, 005930.KS (Taylor), AMKR-class OSAT reshoring — plus every fab-tool maker selling into subsidized shells (AMAT, LRCX, KLAC).
fiscal_programs.note: Reshoring changes geography, not chokepoint ownership — the same names win, in more expensive fabs. Watch a possible CHIPS 2.0 and datacenter-power permitting reform as the AI-era sequels.

fiscal_programs.who: 0981.HK SMIC, 002371.SZ NAURA, 688256.SH Cambricon, 301269.SZ Empyrean, 688234.SH SICC, CXMT (private) — the whole china-localization theme.
fiscal_programs.note: Capital without EUV access: expect capacity in mature nodes + brute-force advanced attempts. Deflationary for mature-node economics globally (our excluded lagging-edge names).

fiscal_programs.who: Rapidus (private, 2nm), TSM Kumamoto JV, 285A.T Kioxia, plus the equipment/materials complex (8035.T, Shin-Etsu, SUMCO) that a domestic fab base feeds.
fiscal_programs.note: Reinforces the japan-chokepoint theme — Japan pays to keep its materials/equipment moat physically at home.

fiscal_programs.who: ASML, AIXA.DE, SMHN.DE, SOI.PA, IFX.DE, ATS.VI, ENR.DE — the 9 records tagged eu-chips-act.
fiscal_programs.note: Pivot from mega-fab dreams to procurement + smaller-country niches — bullish the European equipment/substrate specialists rather than fab shells.

fiscal_programs.who: 000660.KS, 005930.KS + the Korean back-end cohort (Hanmi, Doosan Tesna, SEMCO, LG Innotek, Wonik IPS).
fiscal_programs.note: Underwrites the HBM capex race — and the 'Korea Unlocked' re-rating thesis.

fiscal_programs.who: Demand-side force: buys NVDA/AMD systems, Dell/SMCI/HPE integration, dci power/cooling — a second buyer class beside hyperscalers.
fiscal_programs.note: Fiscal money is less ROI-sensitive than corporate capex — it cushions the froth scenario where hyperscalers pause.

levers.l: FCC import ban on Chinese optical transceivers (drafting)
levers.d: Chinese vendors hold >50% of the global datacenter-transceiver market, InnoLight alone ~27% (Counterpoint). A US import ban on new models would forcibly re-route that demand to COHR, LITE, AAOI, FN, CIEN, NOK, MTSI, SMTC — but the Foundation for American Innovation notes the Western vendors lack the SCALE to replace Chinese supply quickly, so the near-term effect is pricing power and shortage, not clean substitution. Mirror-image risk for 300308.SZ and 300502.SZ. Still drafting — could be modified or shelved.
Renewal = status quo; lapse = magnets/Ga/Ge/chemicals shock into robotics, optics and fab chemicals. The single most dated policy risk on the board.
If entity-lists give way to a China-wide equipment ban, AMAT/LRCX/KLAC/8035.T lose the remaining China backlog; ASML already effectively there on EUV.
Every H-series reclassification swings NVDA/AMD China revenue by $Bs and re-prices Cambricon/Huawei's captive market share in mirror image.
Chip/electronics tariffs would tax the Taiwan-assembled AI supply chain broadly — ODMs and packaged-silicon importers first.
The on/off lever on SNPS/CDNS China revenue (~10-15%) — historically toggled with little warning; Empyrean is the mirror trade.
Retaliation card against US chipmakers with China exposure (MU precedent 2023; NVDA probe on file).
